origins: Fear of being left often begins with real loss: a parent who left, died, or was emotionally absent; a divorce; repeated moves; or a partner who walked away. A child may conclude that people always leave, and that it must be because of something in them. As adults, people with this fear may cling tightly, test others, or avoid closeness altogether, and these patterns can sometimes bring about the very loss they fear.
teaches: Scripture is honest that people do leave, die, and fail us. David even wrote of being forsaken by father and mother. But God promises He will never leave or forsake His people. Isaiah says that even if a mother could forget her nursing child, God will not forget you. Jesus promised not to leave His followers as orphans. Human relationships are precious and uncertain, but there is One who will never walk away. That security can free us to love others without clinging or running.
self_statements: It’s only a matter of time.
If I let someone close, they’ll abandon me.
I have to keep people happy or they’ll go.
I’m easy to walk away from.
I can’t survive being left again.
errors: Predicting that people will leave without evidence.
Believing that because some people left, everyone will.
Assuming people left because something is wrong with me.
Imagining that being left would be unbearable and endless.
questions: Who left me in the past, and what were the real reasons?
Who has stayed in my life, even through hard times?
Am I clinging, testing, or pulling away to protect myself?
What evidence do I have that this person will leave?
What does God promise about His presence?
How could I love more freely if I trusted God’s presence?
truth: Some people have left me, and that was painful. But not everyone leaves, and God never will. He has promised to be with me always. I can love people without clinging or running, because my deepest security is in the One who stays.
hw_truths: God will never leave or forsake me.
My past losses do not predict every future.
Jesus will not leave me an orphan.
log: Each evening, write the names of people who showed up for you today, in large or small ways.
actions: Write the names of people who have stayed in your life through hard times. Thank God for each one.
When you are tempted to test someone’s loyalty, pause and instead tell them honestly what you need.
Give someone space this week without texting or checking in excessively. Notice what happens.
Write Deuteronomy 31:6 on a card and read it whenever you fear being left.
prayer: Lord, I am afraid of losing the people I love. Thank You that You will never leave me or forsake me. Heal the wounds from those who left, help me love without clinging, and let me rest in Your faithful presence. Amen.
